title.narrative: CZI From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation 2023-2027
CZI From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation 2023-2027

description.narrative: Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) "From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation" är ett 3-årigt stöd på 25 miljoner kronor till CZI:s strategi som löper från 2024 till 2028 och som syftar till att stärka dess roll inom policy-forskning och påverkansarbete för ett gynnsamt företagsklimat i Zimbabwe. Genom sitt arbete fungerar CZI kontinuerligt som en viktig mellanhand mellan den offentliga och den privata sektorn. CZI formulerar evidensbaserade policy-förslag, engagerar regeringen i en substantiell och konstruktiv dialog och främjar handel inom och utanför Zimbabwes gränser. Dessutom kommer CZI:s arbete att leda till att företagsutveckling främjas med skapande av arbetstillfällen och entreprenörskap från undersektorn för små och medelstora företag och till minskad import i takt med att affärsförbindelser skapas mellan stora tillverkningsföretag och små och medelstora företag.

Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI)” From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation” is a 3-year strategy support of SEK 25 million to CZI’s strategy running from 2024 to 2028 seeking to strengthen its role in policy research and advocacy of enabling business environment in Zimbabwe. Through its work, CZI continuously works as key intermediary between the public and private sector. It formulates evidence-based policy proposals, engage government in substantive and constructive dialogue and promotion of trade within and beyond Zimbabwe boarders. Furthermore, CZI’s work will result in promotion of enterprise development with job creation and entrepreneurship from the SMEs subsector and reduced imports as business linkages are forged between large manufacturing and small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

Goal Growth and Expansion of inclusive and sustainable economic activities
Objectives To create systemic pro-poor change in the business environment reform system, this project will work to: 1. Curate entrepreneurship opportunities and corresponding conducive environment 2. Create financing opportunities for off-taker backed green field projects 3. Advance Green Manufacturing, Sustainability and Climate Change modelling and phasing for start ups 4. Create a conducive business environment for manufacturing The intervention should result in the strengthening of confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) in its role and in creating sustainable, systemic change in the business environment.

Curate Entrepreneurship Opportunities and a Corresponding Conducive Environment
Significant progress was made in identifying and promoting entrepreneurship opportunities through the implementation of the Five-Year Industry Agenda and the Manufacturing for Manufacturing initiative. Feasibility studies and value chain analyses identified viable entrepreneurial opportunities in sectors such as enzymes, gelatin, glucose production, and cotton farm-gate ginning, creating pathways for local enterprise development and import substitution.
CZI strengthened the entrepreneurship ecosystem by launching the Entrepreneurship Ecosystem Forum, which brought together government, industry, academia, financial institutions, and start-ups to develop a coordinated national entrepreneurship agenda. This demonstrated a structured approach to identifying entrepreneurship opportunities linked to industrial demaind. Key outcomes included the establishment of a Working Party, development of a proposed Zimbabwe Start-up Act, and conceptualisation of financing mechanisms such as a Venture Fund and diaspora investment platforms.
Furthermore, entrepreneurship training on the Electronic Government Procurement (EGP) System equipped SMEs with skills to access public procurement opportunities, while market linkage initiatives resulted in tangible business opportunities, including a USD 24,000 corporate gifting contract secured by a local SME through CZI's promotion programme.
However, systematic reporting on outcomes such as number of enterprises supported into new markets, sustained jobs, or scaling of startups remains limited.
Create a conducive business environment for manufacturing
Substantial progress was achieved in improving the manufacturing operating environment through evidence-based advocacy, policy engagement, and regulatory reform initiatives. CZI successfully translated member concerns into policy action through structured engagements with government institutions and standing committees. Second-year results demonstrate clear and credible policy and regulatory outcomes, including legislative changes, institutionalisation of regulatory impact assessment, and measurable improvements in regulatory processes. These reforms are already embedded within government systems and are unlikely to be undermined by the reduced final year.
A major achievement was CZI's leadership role in the development of the Zimbabwe National Industrial Development Policy 2 (ZNIDP2) and its contribution to the Zimbabwe Industrial Reconstruction and Growth Plan (ZIRGP), where several industry proposals were adopted, including Manufacturing for Manufacturing, local content development, and manufacturing finance initiatives. CZI championed Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA), leading to Cabinet approval for its adoption and contributing to ongoing efforts to reduce regulatory costs, which had been identified as accounting for approximately 18% of business overheads. These interventions strengthened industry competitiveness and improved the ease of doing business for manufacturers.
CZI made sustained engagements between 2023 and 2025 through monthly inflation and currency reports, the 2023 Monetary Policy submission, the 2024 National Budget on pricing distortions arising from the enforcement of an administratively determined exchange rate. This resulted in the repeal of Statutory Instrument 81A of 2024 and the introduction of a market-determined exchange rate framework under SI 34 of 2025. As these measures took effect during 2025, pricing distortions were reduced, and USD inflation began to ease.
Create financing opportunities for off-taker backed green field projects
CZI identified emerging manufacturers with strong industrial promise which could be linked to manufacturing gaps in value chains such as glucose, cellulose and gang nails which are currently being imported. The SMEs were offered free membership, connecting them to networks to foster exposure to established firms and gain access to knowledge and training. They were supported in their readiness for trade and investments with programmes like AfCFTA Protocol on Women in Trade which provided practical insight into how entrepreneurs can become investment and trade ready.
Moreover, conversations were initiated with value chain anchors to assess their interest in partnering with SMEs. However, progress has remained largely preparatory, focusing on dialogue, and exploration of potential financing mechanisms. Financing outcomes require extended time horizons to allow for pipeline development, due diligence, risk allocation, and deal closure. With the reduced timeline in 2026, CZI might end up with clearer financing concepts, and strengthened relationships, but without completed greenfield projects.
Advance Green Manufacturing-Sustainability and Climate Change modelling and phasing for start ups
CZI has made credible progress in integrating sustainability considerations into research, policy discourse, and institutional forums, and in building awareness around green industrialization. Research outputs focused on climate finance, green industrialization, green jobs, and skills development, providing evidence-based frameworks to support sustainable manufacturing growth.
The Sustainable Business Committee promoted initiatives on energy efficiency, climate action, circular economy practices, waste management, and sustainability regulation. The Strategic Intelligence Forum further strengthened awareness of sustainability as a competitiveness driver by incorporating dedicated discussions on sustainability, digital transformation, and future-ready business models.
Additionally, engagement with development partners and institutions on climate-related initiatives contributed to the development of policy and investment frameworks that support the gradual integration of sustainability principles into start-up and manufacturing ecosystems.
These are important foundational steps and are likely to be further consolidated by the end of the project. However, applied outcomes such as start-up level climate modelling, phased transition pathways, or implementation of green manufacturing pilots require time for design, testing, and enterprise adoption and results for these might remain limited due to reduced implementation time for the final year.
Financial and Audit Report
The financial statements for 2025 were prepared in a way to mirror the approved budget allowing for direct comparison using accrual basis and they were signed by the management. The closing balance from 2024 matched the opening balances for 2025. CZI does not forward funds to third parties and funds were used for CZI core activities. CZI received SEK 8 000 000 during the reporting period which translated to $858 537 and cumulatively they had available funds for 2025 amounting to US$ 1 545 581. They incurred expenditures amounting to US$ 1 022 964 and had a cash balance of US$ 522 617 as per bank balance. The bank balance agreed with financial information as presented by CZI. They rolled over US$ 93 260 into the 2026 budget and were factored in the revised budget.
The independent audit report provided an opinion stating that the financial statements presented a true and fair view of the financial position of the CZI core support for the year ending December 31, 2025.
Lessons Learned
-Evidence-based advocacy is more effective when grounded in member experiences and supported by credible research. CZI was able to convert firm-level challenges into actionable policy recommendations such as the adoption of Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA), inclusion of industry priorities in national planning processes, and uptake of proposals within the Zimbabwe Industrial Reconstruction and Growth Plan.
-Entrepreneurship development requires a coordinated ecosystem rather than isolated interventions. The discussions around the proposed Start-up Act, Venture Fund, and Zimbabwe Integrated Entrepreneurship and Startup (ZIES) Framework demonstrated that sustainable enterprise growth is best supported through coordinated ecosystem approaches that address policy, financing, market access, and capacity-building simultaneously.
Adaptations Made by CZI
-Transition from traditional advocacy to a policy partnership model with government: CZI adapted its approach from being primarily a stakeholder consulted on policy issues to becoming an active policy development partner through its leadership role in developing the Zimbabwe National Industrial Development Policy 2 (ZNIDP2) and the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce. This adaptation enabled deeper engagement in policy formulation and increased the uptake of industry recommendations within government programmes and strategies.
-Expansion of institutional capacity and creation of specialized platforms to address emerging priorities. CZI adapted by strengthening its internal technical capacity and creating new specialized platforms due to the evolving needs of the industry. The Industrial and Economic Research Unit was expanded from five to eight economists, including three PhD-level researchers, resulting in a significant increase in research outputs. In addition, CZI established the Trade and Regulatory Affairs Desk, introduced the DigiTech and AI for Business Initiative, and expanded sustainability-focused programming. These enabled CZI to address emerging issues such as digital transformation, artificial intelligence, climate finance, export readiness, and regulatory reform while remaining responsive to member needs.
Conclusion
CZI continues to demonstrate strong institutional capacity, sound financial management, and a credible role as a policy convener and ecosystem builder within Zimbabwes manufacturing and entrepreneurship landscape. The year 2025 showed progress towards CZI positioning and strengthening demonstrated by:
Influence through participation in structured policy formulation processes Opinion and Knowledge Leadership through the shaping of industrial discourse and reform direction. Legitimacy through formal recognition within national and sectoral platforms. Credibility through the expansion and external utilisation of research outputs. Relevance through alignment with real-time industrial constraints Effectiveness through measurable outputs and policy uptake.
Key recommendations going forward include:
-CZI to demonstrate concrete financial mobilisation results for off-taker-backed and greenfield manufacturing projects, including deal volumes and capital leveraged.
-CZI to have a clearer translation of systemic reforms into measurable enterprise-level results, particularly for SMEs and green start-ups .
